unit.why: A short anecdote told by the Neskhiz rebbe about being rebuked by his father as a child for drinking against his instruction.
unit.boundary_note: the closing heading 'מענין דיבור' belongs to the next division

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ ז״ט וז״ל סיפר מרן נעסכיז
stories.end_quote: הדברים היטב אל לבבי שלא לשוכחם
stories.summary_en: The Neskhiz rebbe recalled that as a child he drank after eating fish against his father's order to wait. His father rebuked him: if he could not master a small craving now, how would he master greater desires later? He wept and kept the lesson all his life.

tags.why: The tzaddik's father is the rebuking character.
Mastering desire is the story's point.
The child disobeys his father's instruction.
He is told not to drink and violates the instruction.
The lesson is about overcoming cravings.

quotes: ושמתי את דברי על לבבי לזכרון תמיד
tags.why: He weeps and takes the rebuke to heart for good.
The story is framed as told by a named tzaddik.
Drinking after fish is probably a customary drink, but the text does not specify the drink.
No women appear in the story; this is the closest available women label.
